# E077 - Christopher Doyle

## Metadata
- **Document ID:** E077
- **Brand/Company:** Christopher Doyle (personal brand / design satire)
- **Industry:** Design/Branding Agency
- **Year:** 2008
- **File Size:** 1.0 MB
- **Page Count:** 18
- **Document Type:** Brand Identity Guidelines (satirical/conceptual)
- **Software:** Adobe InDesign CS3
- **Format:** Landscape (1133 x 751 pts)

## Brand Strategy
A conceptual piece in which Australian designer Christopher Doyle applies corporate brand guidelines to himself as a person. The document is structured identically to a real brand manual but every element refers to the designer's physical appearance, personality, and lifestyle. Core values center on consistency, evolution, and authenticity -- delivered through humor and self-awareness. The framing is clever: it demonstrates the designer's understanding of branding by treating his own identity as a brand system.

## Logo
The "logo" is Christopher Doyle himself, presented in photographic form. Four key identity formats are defined:
- **Full Colour Vertical** (preferred/most common -- standing)
- **Full Colour Seated_Casual**
- **Full Colour Seated_Formal**
- **Full Colour Vertical_Private** (requires direct permission; not for public use)
All formats can also appear in black and white (mono).

## Typography
No dedicated typography section visible. The document itself uses a clean, modern sans-serif layout consistent with mid-2000s design agency aesthetics. Section headers use lowercase with underscores ("colour palette", "clearance space").

## Color
- **Core palette:** 100% black (must be present at all times -- refers to hair/clothing)
- **Secondary palette:** Variable, must complement core palette, reference seasonal change. No transparency allowed.
- **Key constraint:** Hair and skin colors cannot change.
- **Mono format:** 100% black retained; overuse of black can slim the identity; excess white discouraged.
- Color variations are presented as different outfit/styling combinations.

## Graphics / Visual Language
- **Graphic devices:** Band (headband) and Spectacles -- accessories used as consistent visual identity elements
- **Clearance space:** Personal space around the identity must be maintained, based on width of the identity. Exception: in the company of "Sarah_Full Colour Vertical"
- **Minimum size:** 89cm (minimum height); 183cm (maximum/most common height). Width may vary.

## Photography
Photography by Ian Haigh. All identity presentations are photographic. The document uses full-body portrait photography as the primary visual language, shot on neutral backgrounds in a style mimicking logo usage guidelines.

## Applications
- **Wayfinding:** Hand gestures for directional guidance, used when verbal directions are insufficient
- **Sustainability:** Vegetarian diet, recycled materials, secondhand/vintage clothing, public transport, energy-efficient appliances
- **Incorrect use:** "Tucking" and "Tying" (shirt modifications) shown as identity misuse, paralleling logo misuse sections

## Tone of Voice
Defined as "loud and clear." Equal parts cynicism and positivity. Uses the "I think" rule -- critical statements must begin with "I..." to take ownership and soften delivery. Coarse language permitted when contextually appropriate (e.g., discussing Nickelback) but never in presence of "Mum_Full Colour Vertical." Humor is central to the verbal identity.

## Outliers / Unique Elements
- This is a satirical/conceptual brand guidelines document -- the entire piece is a creative exercise treating a human being as a brand. It is not a traditional set of brand guidelines.
- The document functions as a portfolio piece demonstrating the designer's mastery of brand guidelines structure and conventions.
- The humor is consistent and well-crafted: "Full Colour Vertical_Private" requires permission and should never appear in public; clearance space exceptions for a romantic partner; sustainability "don'ts" with asterisks noting they are "at times unavoidable."
- Printed on 100% recycled stock (Envirocare).

## Quality Score
**3/5** -- As a brand guidelines document, it is structurally complete and well-organized with a proper table of contents, clear sections, and consistent formatting. However, it contains no real typographic specifications, no actual color values (hex/CMYK/Pantone), and no usable design system. Its value is primarily as a creative/conceptual reference demonstrating how brand guidelines conventions can be applied inventively. The writing quality and wit are high.
